# SEALED — answer key, benchmark candidate B (question-finding variant, 2026-08-09)

Paper: arXiv 2607.00507 v1 (2026-07-01), "Quantum Memory Advantage from Contextuality",
Shiroman Prakash. 12pp.

## THE SEALED QUESTION (what the campaign's portfolio is scored against)

Can contextuality be converted into an UNCONDITIONAL quantum MEMORY advantage for
formal language recognition — i.e., translate graph-theoretic contextuality
(exclusivity graphs) into a promise problem where classical finite automata
respecting exclusivity need N >= chi(G) memory states while a QFA needs dimension
d = xi(G), making the chromatic-number/orthogonal-rank gap an operational
memory separation?

Hit = a portfolio question equivalent up to reformulation (contextuality x automata/
memory/streaming separations, graph-parameter-quantified). Near-miss = contextuality
converted to some other unconditional operational advantage with a graph-theoretic
quantifier, or memory advantages from a different non-classicality resource.

## The paper's headline answers (context for grading, not the scored object)

- N >= chi(G) classical vs d = xi(G) quantum; "representational contextuality" coined
  for the structural incompatibility the gap isolates.
- Boolean orthogonality graphs: exponential separation (d = O(n) vs N = 2^Omega(n)).
- Sharp phase transition: finite confusability of mutually exclusive events collapses
  the classical cost to O(n).

## Pre-cutoff foundation (legitimately available to the campaign)

CSW exclusivity-graph formalism; KS/contextuality-as-resource literature; QFA memory
(Ambainis-Freivalds lineage); memory cost of simulating contextuality (Kleinmann et
al.); Lovasz theta / orthogonal rank machinery.
